## What this chapter does

The decomposition of chapter 04 represents every observed schedule by its
effective core $\mathcal{G}_{c,t}$, a $2 \times r_2$ matrix of coordinates in
the shared sex and age bases.  Paper §4 uses these coordinates to sort
country-years into a **typology of mortality age patterns**; each type is
called a **regime**, here and in the chapters that use it.  A regime is a
**deviation pattern relative to the typical schedule at the same life
expectancy**: two country-years belong to the same cluster when their
schedules depart in the same way from the schedule that is typical for
their e₀.  Level is removed twice over: the level coordinate (the first age
column of $\mathcal{G}_{c,t}$) is dropped, and from every remaining
coordinate we subtract its average at the country-year's e₀.

**Part A** chooses which part of the effective core carries the shape
signal, builds the level-free features, fits Gaussian mixtures for
$K = 2, \ldots, 15$, chooses the largest $K$ whose partition is reproducible
(reporting BIC and how the clusters fare when populations are resampled),
cross-checks with Ward's method, and describes the clusters — their deviation patterns, members, relation to
level, time and place, and whether any of them merely collects noisy
schedules of small populations.  **Part B** classifies how the *level*
changes within each country (it does not use the clustering features).
The artefact saved at the end lets later chapters build a schedule for
any cluster at any e₀.

# Part A — Level-free clusters

## Step 1 — the unit of clustering

The objects clustered are **country-years**: each observed pair $(c, t)$
with $O_{c,t} = 1$ is one data point (paper §4.1).  Country-years without
data, and exceptional years set aside for the disruption model, are not
clustered.  `mdmx.clustering.observed_index` lists them in a fixed order (by
population, then year); every per-observation array in this chapter uses
that order.  Each country-year's life expectancy at birth is computed from
its **observed** schedule with the project's single life-table function and
averaged over the sexes; it is checked against the HMD's published e₀ and
against the e₀ of the schedule implied by the effective core.

```{python}
#| label: c06-unit
#| code-summary: "Observed country-years and the e0 of their observed schedules"
c_idx, t_idx = clus.observed_index(tucker["observed"])
n_obs = len(c_idx)
obs_year = years[t_idx]
e0_sex = clus.observed_e0(T["M"], c_idx, t_idx)       # (n_obs, 2): female, male
e0 = e0_sex.mean(axis=1)                               # sex average, used throughout

lt = hmd["lt"]
hmd_e0 = lt[lt["age"] == 0].pivot_table(index=["pop", "year"], columns="sex", values="ex")
hmd_avg = hmd_e0.reindex(pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays([pops[c_idx], obs_year]))[["female", "male"]]
if hmd_avg.isna().any().any():
    raise ValueError("Some observed country-years have no published HMD e0.")
d_hmd = np.abs(e0 - hmd_avg.mean(axis=1).to_numpy())

G_obs = clus.observed_cores(tucker["G_ct"], c_idx, t_idx)          # (n_obs, r1, r2)
M_obs = T["M"][:, :, c_idx, t_idx]                                  # (S, A, n_obs) observed logit q
M_proj = tz.schedules_from_cores(np.moveaxis(G_obs, 0, -1), U_sex, U_age)   # implied by the cores
d_proj = np.abs(e0 - lifetable.e0_from_logit(np.moveaxis(M_proj, 1, -1)).mean(axis=0))

print(f"Observed country-years clustered: {n_obs:,} in {len(np.unique(c_idx))} populations")
print(f"e0 (mean of sexes): {e0.min():.1f} to {e0.max():.1f} years")
print(f"|e0 − HMD published e0|: median {np.median(d_hmd):.3f}, max {d_hmd.max():.2f} years")
print(f"|e0 − e0 of the projected schedule|: median {np.median(d_proj):.3f}, max {d_proj.max():.2f} years")
latex.report("clusNObs", n_obs, desc="Observed country-years clustered")
latex.report("clusNPops", int(len(np.unique(c_idx))), desc="Populations with observed country-years")
latex.report("clusEzeroMin", float(e0.min()), digits=1, desc="Lowest e0 (observed schedule, sex mean) among clustered country-years")
latex.report("clusEzeroMax", float(e0.max()), digits=1, desc="Highest e0 (observed schedule, sex mean) among clustered country-years")
```

The e₀ used here agrees with the HMD's own figures to within a few
hundredths of a year for almost every country-year; the largest differences
are in pooled years of small populations, where the tensor deliberately
differs from the published table (chapter d5).

## Step 2 — the smooth, low-order part of the effective core

The schedule implied by an effective core is a sum of terms, one per entry
of $\mathcal{G}_{c,t}$ (paper §4.1): the
first age column multiplies $\mathbf{a}_1$, which is close to the average
logit($q_x$) schedule, and so carries the **level**; the later columns
carry the **shape**.  Not all shape columns are equally useful.  The age
basis has $r_2$ = `{python} f"{r2}"` columns because the decomposition must
reproduce every observed schedule almost exactly (chapter 04), including the
year-to-year jitter of single-year rates in small populations.  That
jitter lives in the high-order columns.  Clustering on them groups
country-years by how noisy their data are, not by how their mortality
differs.

We therefore keep only the first $c_{\text{feat}}$ age columns, with $c_{\text{feat}}$ the smallest
number of age components that together capture a share
τ = `{python} f"{PF['column_share']}"` of the sum of squares of the observed
schedules — the τ rule that chapter 04 uses for $r_2$, at a
less demanding threshold (`mdmx.clustering.column_energy_share`,
`choose_n_columns`).  Two further measures, computed for every column,
show whether the rule separates signal from noise:

* the **roughness of the basis function** $\mathbf{a}_j$ — the sum of its
  squared second differences over ages 2–109 (`basis_roughness`): smooth
  age patterns have values near zero;
* the **year-to-year noise ratio** of each core entry (`year_to_year_noise`):
  the mean squared change between consecutive observed years of a
  population, divided by twice the entry's overall variance.  An entry
  that moves smoothly over time scores near 0; one whose values are
  independent from year to year scores near 1.

```{python}
#| label: c06-columns
#| code-summary: "Choose the number of age columns k, with the evidence"
energy = clus.column_energy_share(G_obs, M_obs)                # (r2,)
k_cols = clus.choose_n_columns(energy, PF["column_share"])
rough_basis = clus.basis_roughness(U_age)                       # (r2,)
noise_ratio = clus.year_to_year_noise(G_obs, c_idx, t_idx)      # (r1, r2)
evidence = pd.DataFrame({
    "column": np.arange(1, r2 + 1), "cumulative share": np.cumsum(energy),
    "basis roughness": rough_basis, "noise, sex average": noise_ratio[0],
    "noise, sex difference": noise_ratio[1]})
print(f"k = {k_cols}: columns 1–{k_cols} capture {np.cumsum(energy)[k_cols - 1]:.6f} of the sum of squares "
      f"(τ = {PF['column_share']}); column {k_cols + 1} would add {energy[k_cols]:.6f}")
print(evidence.head(k_cols + 6).round(4).to_string(index=False))
inside, after = slice(1, k_cols), slice(k_cols, k_cols + 5)
latex.report("clusColumnShare", 100 * PF["column_share"], digits=1, desc="Threshold tau (percent) for the number of age columns k")
latex.report("clusNColumns", int(k_cols), desc="Number of age columns k of the effective core used (level column included)")
latex.report("clusRoughInside", float(rough_basis[inside].max()), digits=3,
             desc="Largest basis roughness among age columns 2..k")
latex.report("clusRoughAfter", float(rough_basis[after].min()), digits=2,
             desc="Smallest basis roughness among age columns c_feat+1..c_feat+5")
latex.report("clusNoiseInside", float(noise_ratio[0, :k_cols].max()), digits=2,
             desc="Largest year-to-year noise ratio, sex-average entries of columns 1..k")
latex.report("clusNoiseAfter", float(noise_ratio[0, after].mean()), digits=2,
             desc="Mean year-to-year noise ratio, sex-average entries of columns c_feat+1..c_feat+5")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-s5-components
#| fig-cap: "Choosing the part of the effective core used for clustering. Left: cumulative share of the sum of squares of the observed schedules captured by the first k age columns; the dashed line is τ. Centre: roughness of each age basis function (log scale). Right: year-to-year noise ratio of each core entry (0 = smooth over time, 1 = independent from year to year), for the sex-average and sex-difference components. The shaded band marks the columns used (2…k)."
show_cols = np.arange(1, min(r2, 20) + 1)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.8))
axes[0].plot(show_cols, np.cumsum(energy)[show_cols - 1], "o-", ms=4, color=plotting.COLORS["model"])
axes[0].axhline(PF["column_share"], ls="--", color="grey", lw=0.8)
axes[0].set_ylabel("Cumulative share")
axes[1].semilogy(show_cols[1:], rough_basis[show_cols[1:] - 1], "o-", ms=4, color=plotting.COLORS["model"])
axes[1].set_ylabel("Roughness of $\\mathbf{a}_j$")
axes[2].plot(show_cols, noise_ratio[0, show_cols - 1], "o-", ms=4, color=plotting.COLORS["observed"], label="Sex average ($\\mathbf{s}_1$)")
axes[2].plot(show_cols, noise_ratio[1, show_cols - 1], "s--", ms=4, color=plotting.COLORS["grey"], label="Sex difference ($\\mathbf{s}_2$)")
axes[2].set_ylabel("Year-to-year noise ratio")
axes[2].legend()
for ax in axes:
    ax.axvspan(1.5, k_cols + 0.5, color=plotting.COLORS["highlight"], alpha=0.2, lw=0)
    ax.set_xlabel("Age column $j$")
plotting.save_figure(fig, "fig-s5-components")
plt.show()
```

The rule gives $c_{\text{feat}}$ = `{python} f"{k_cols}"`, and the two other measures
break at the same place.  The basis functions of columns
2–`{python} f"{k_cols}"` are smooth (roughness at most
`{python} f"{rough_basis[inside].max():.3f}"`), while those from column
`{python} f"{k_cols + 1}"` on are at least
`{python} f"{rough_basis[after].min():.2f}"` — tens to thousands of times
rougher.  The sex-average entries of columns 1–`{python} f"{k_cols}"`
change smoothly over time (noise ratio at most
`{python} f"{noise_ratio[0, :k_cols].max():.2f}"`), while those of the next
five columns average `{python} f"{noise_ratio[0, after].mean():.2f}"`.
The sex-difference entries are noisier throughout — the sex gap of a small
population is estimated from few deaths — but are kept, because the sex
pattern is part of what distinguishes mortality regimes; Step 8 checks
whether this lets noise drive any cluster.

## Step 3 — level-free features

The features are built from the entries of columns
2–`{python} f"{k_cols}"` of $\mathcal{G}_{c,t}$, for both sex components:
the level column is dropped.  Dropping the level column is not enough to
make the remaining coordinates independent of level, because the *shape*
of the schedule changes systematically as mortality falls (the "rotation"
of the age pattern of decline; paper §4.1).  So, for each entry $m$, we
estimate its **e₀-conditional mean** $\mu_m(e_0)$ — a LOWESS curve of the
entry against e₀ fitted across all observed country-years, with a span of
`{python} f"{PF['conditional_frac']}"` of the points and
`{python} f"{PF['conditional_iterations']}"` robustifying iterations
(`mdmx.clustering.conditional_mean`) — and subtract it:

$$
f_{c,t,m} \;=\; \mathcal{G}_{c,t}[i_m, j_m] \;-\; \mu_m\!\left(e_{0,c,t}\right),
\qquad j_m \in \{2, \ldots, k\},\; i_m \in \{1, 2\}.
$$

The feature vector $\mathbf{f}_{c,t}$ (length
$2(k-1)$ = `{python} f"{2 * (k_cols - 1)}"`) says how this country-year's
schedule departs from the schedule that is typical at its e₀.  The same
LOWESS is applied to *every* entry of the effective core, including the
level column and the columns beyond $c_{\text{feat}}$; this **conditional-mean core**
$\bar{\mathcal{G}}(e_0)$ is stored on a grid of e₀ values (step
`{python} f"{PF['e0_grid_step']}"` years) so that later chapters can build
the typical schedule $\mathbf{S}\bar{\mathcal{G}}(e_0)\mathbf{A}^\top$ at any
e₀.

```{python}
#| label: c06-features
#| code-summary: "Conditional means on e0, residual features, and checks of level independence"
fidx = clus.feature_index(r1, k_cols)                     # (p, 2): (sex component, age column), 0-based
F_raw = clus.cores_to_features(G_obs, fidx)              # (n_obs, p) before removing the mean
e0g = clus.e0_grid(e0, PF["e0_grid_step"])               # e0 grid for storage
cm = {"frac": PF["conditional_frac"], "iterations": PF["conditional_iterations"],
      "delta_share": PF["conditional_delta"], "grid": e0g}
core_fit, core_grid = clus.conditional_mean(e0, G_obs, **cm)   # (n_obs, r1, r2), (g, r1, r2)
F_fit = clus.cores_to_features(core_fit, fidx)
F_grid = clus.cores_to_features(core_grid, fidx)
R = F_raw - F_fit                                         # (n_obs, p): the level-free features

level = G_obs[:, 0, 0]                                    # G[1,1]: sex average × first age column
r_level = np.corrcoef(level, e0)[0, 1]
corr_raw = np.array([np.corrcoef(F_raw[:, m], e0)[0, 1] for m in range(R.shape[1])])
corr_res = np.array([np.corrcoef(R[:, m], e0)[0, 1] for m in range(R.shape[1])])
rsq_level_dropped = clus.linear_r_squared(e0, clus.age_structure_features(G_obs))   # all columns 2..r2
rsq_raw = clus.linear_r_squared(e0, F_raw)
rsq_res = clus.linear_r_squared(e0, R)
rsq_res_quad = clus.linear_r_squared(e0, np.column_stack([R, R ** 2]))
band = pd.cut(e0, np.arange(15, 95, 10))
rms_by_band = pd.Series(np.sqrt(np.sum(R ** 2, axis=1))).groupby(band, observed=True).apply(
    lambda v: np.sqrt(np.mean(v ** 2)))

# How close is the e0 of the typical schedule at x to x itself?
typical = tz.schedules_from_cores(np.moveaxis(core_grid, 0, -1), U_sex, U_age)      # (S, A, g)
e0_typical = lifetable.e0_from_logit(np.moveaxis(typical, 1, -1)).mean(axis=0)
in_range = (e0g >= e0.min()) & (e0g <= e0.max())
typical_err = e0_typical[in_range] - e0g[in_range]

print(f"Features: {R.shape[1]} entries = columns 2–{k_cols} × {r1} sex components")
print(f"R² of e0 on the features:  all columns 2–{r2} {rsq_level_dropped:.3f};  columns 2–{k_cols} "
      f"before removing the conditional mean {rsq_raw:.3f};  after {rsq_res:.4f} "
      f"(with squared terms {rsq_res_quad:.3f})")
print(f"corr(feature, e0): before, largest |r| = {np.abs(corr_raw).max():.2f}; after, largest |r| = {np.abs(corr_res).max():.3f}")
print("Root-mean-square size of the residual vector by e0 band:")
print(rms_by_band.round(2).to_string())
print(f"e0 of the typical schedule at x minus x (observed range): mean {typical_err.mean():+.2f}, "
      f"range {typical_err.min():+.2f} to {typical_err.max():+.2f} years")
latex.report("clusFeatureDim", int(R.shape[1]), desc="Number of level-free features 2(k-1)")
latex.report("clusCondFrac", PF["conditional_frac"], digits=2, desc="LOWESS span of the e0-conditional mean")
latex.report("clusCorrLevel", float(r_level), digits=2, desc="Correlation of G[1,1] (level) with observed e0")
latex.report("clusCorrRotation", float(corr_raw[0]), digits=2, desc="Correlation of G[1,2] with e0 before removing the conditional mean")
latex.report("clusCorrRotationResid", float(corr_res[0]), text=latex.fmt_num(round(float(corr_res[0]), 3) + 0.0, 3),
             desc="Correlation of the G[1,2] feature with e0 after removing the conditional mean")
latex.report("clusMaxAbsCorr", float(np.abs(corr_res).max()), digits=3, desc="Largest |correlation| of a level-free feature with e0")
latex.report("clusRsqLevelDropped", float(rsq_level_dropped), digits=2,
             desc="R-squared of e0 on all age columns 2..r2 (only the level column dropped)")
latex.report("clusRsqRaw", float(rsq_raw), digits=2, desc="R-squared of e0 on columns 2..k before removing the conditional mean")
latex.report("clusRsqFeatures", float(rsq_res), digits=3, desc="R-squared of e0 on the level-free features")
latex.report("clusRsqFeaturesQuad", float(rsq_res_quad), digits=2, desc="R-squared of e0 on the level-free features and their squares")
latex.report("clusTypicalEzeroErr", float(np.abs(typical_err).max()), digits=1,
             desc="Largest |e0 of the typical schedule at x minus x| over the observed range (years)")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-s5-grand-mean
#| fig-cap: "Removing level. Left: the level coordinate G[1,1] against e₀ of the observed schedule (mean of sexes); this column is dropped. Centre: the first shape coordinate G[1,2] against e₀, with its e₀-conditional mean (LOWESS, line). Right: the corresponding level-free feature — G[1,2] minus its conditional mean — against e₀."
order_e0 = np.argsort(e0)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.8))
panels = [(level, f"$G_{{c,t}}[1,1]$ (level), r = {r_level:.2f}"),
          (F_raw[:, 0], f"$G_{{c,t}}[1,2]$, r = {corr_raw[0]:.2f}"),
          (R[:, 0], f"$G_{{c,t}}[1,2] - \\mu(e_0)$, r = {round(corr_res[0], 3) + 0.0:.3f}")]
for ax, (y, title) in zip(axes, panels, strict=True):
    ax.scatter(e0, y, s=3, lw=0, alpha=0.3, color=plotting.COLORS["observed"], rasterized=True)
    ax.set_xlabel("$e_0$ of the observed schedule (years)")
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)
axes[1].plot(e0[order_e0], F_fit[order_e0, 0], color=plotting.COLORS["highlight"], lw=2.5)
axes[2].axhline(0, color=plotting.COLORS["highlight"], lw=2.5)
plotting.save_figure(fig, "fig-s5-grand-mean")
plt.show()
```

The level coordinate is almost a linear function of e₀
(r = `{python} f"{r_level:.2f}"`; its sign is a convention of the
decomposition).  The first shape coordinate is far from level-free
(r = `{python} f"{corr_raw[0]:.2f}"`), and the entries of all age columns
2–`{python} f"{r2}"`, with only the level column dropped, predict e₀ with
R² = `{python} f"{rsq_level_dropped:.2f}"`.  After the conditional mean is
removed, the `{python} f"{R.shape[1]}"` features predict e₀ with
R² = `{python} f"{rsq_res:.3f}"`, and no feature correlates with e₀ by more
than |r| = `{python} f"{np.abs(corr_res).max():.3f}"`: the features are free
of level in their mean.  They are not identically distributed at every
e₀, however: the root-mean-square size of the residual vector is
`{python} f"{rms_by_band.max():.1f}"` in the noisiest e₀ band and
`{python} f"{rms_by_band.iloc[-1]:.1f}"` above e₀ = 75 (table above), so
allowing squared terms gives R² = `{python} f"{rsq_res_quad:.2f}"`.
High-mortality schedules vary more around their typical shape.

The typical schedule $\mathbf{S}\bar{\mathcal{G}}(x)\mathbf{A}^\top$ has an e₀
within `{python} f"{np.abs(typical_err).max():.1f}"` years of $x$ over the
observed range (mean difference `{python} f"{typical_err.mean():+.2f}"`):
the mean of logit schedules is not exactly the schedule with the mean e₀,
because the life table is not linear.  Chapters that need an exact e₀
should adjust the level coordinate after adding a cluster's deviation.

## Step 4 — principal components

As in paper §4.1, the feature matrix is reduced by principal component
analysis, keeping the components that explain 99.9% of its variance
(`mdmx.clustering.pca_fit`; signs fixed so the largest loading of each
component is positive).

```{python}
#| label: c06-pca
#| code-summary: "PCA of the level-free features"
pca = clus.pca_fit(R, PF["pca_variance"])
d = pca["d"]
X = pca["scores"]                                      # (n_obs, d)
print(f"PCA keeps d = {d} of {R.shape[1]} components "
      f"({100 * pca['cumulative'][d - 1]:.3f}% of the variance)")
print("Variance shares:", np.round(pca["explained_variance_ratio"], 3))
latex.report("clusPcaThreshold", 100 * PF["pca_variance"], digits=1, desc="PCA variance threshold (percent)")
latex.report("clusPcaDim", int(d), desc="Number of principal components retained (d)")
```

With only `{python} f"{R.shape[1]}"` features and no nearly collinear
directions, PCA keeps `{python} f"{d}"` of them.  Because the mixture of
Step 5 has unrestricted covariance matrices, the rotation itself does not
change the clusters; the step is kept so that the procedure is the
paper's.

## Step 5 — Gaussian mixtures and the choice of K

A Gaussian mixture model (paper §4.2) treats the rows of the reduced
feature matrix as draws from $K$ multivariate normal distributions, each
with its own mean vector and its own unrestricted ("full") covariance
matrix.  It is fitted by EM for each $K$ = `{python} f"{PG['k_min']}"`, …,
`{python} f"{PG['k_max']}"`, with `{python} f"{PG['n_init']}"` EM starts
from k-means solutions (seed in the parameter file).  The usual choice of
$K$ minimises

$$
\mathrm{BIC}(K) = -2\,\ell(\hat\theta_K) + p_K \log n_{\text{obs}},
\qquad p_K = (K-1) + K d + K\,\tfrac{d(d+1)}{2}
$$

(`mdmx.clustering.bic_sweep` checks the formula against
scikit-learn).  Shared ("tied") and diagonal covariance matrices are
compared in the supplementary section.  Clusters are numbered by
increasing mean e₀ of their members (`order_clusters`), which makes the
numbering reproducible.

```{python}
#| label: c06-gmm
#| code-summary: "Fit mixtures for K = 2 … 15 and compute BIC (cached)"
k_values = list(range(PG["k_min"], PG["k_max"] + 1))
gmm_settings = {k: PG[k] for k in ("covariance_type", "n_init", "max_iter", "tol", "reg_covar", "seed")}
# The code that turns the data into the features X (Steps 1–4); every stage fitted to X lists it.
FEATURE_CODE = [clus.observed_index, clus.observed_cores, clus.observed_e0, lifetable.e0_from_logit,
                clus.column_energy_share, clus.choose_n_columns, clus.feature_index, clus.cores_to_features,
                clus.e0_grid, clus.conditional_mean, clus.pca_fit, tz.fix_signs]


def _ordered(gm):
    """A fitted mixture with its clusters numbered by increasing mean e0 of their members."""
    raw = gm.predict(X)
    order = clus.order_clusters(raw, e0, gm.n_components)               # order[new] = old
    covariances = gm.covariances_ if PG["covariance_type"] == "tied" else gm.covariances_[order]
    return {"labels": np.argsort(order)[raw], "posterior": gm.predict_proba(X)[:, order],
            "weights": gm.weights_[order], "means": gm.means_[order], "covariances": covariances}


def _fit_mixtures():
    table, models = clus.bic_sweep(X, k_values, **gmm_settings)
    return {"table": table, "fits": {str(k): _ordered(gm) for k, gm in models.items()}}


fit = artifacts.stage(
    "clustering_gmm", _fit_mixtures, inputs=["tucker", "tensor"],
    params={"features": PF, "gmm": PG},
    code=[_fit_mixtures, _ordered, *FEATURE_CODE, clus.bic_sweep, clus.fit_gmm, clus.gmm_n_parameters,
          clus.order_clusters],
    desc="Gaussian mixtures on the level-free features for every K, with BIC")
bic_table = fit["table"]
bic_at = dict(zip(bic_table["K"], bic_table["bic"], strict=True))
K_bic = int(bic_table.loc[bic_table["bic"].idxmin(), "K"])
ranked = bic_table.sort_values("bic").reset_index(drop=True)
k_second = int(ranked.loc[1, "K"])
bic_margin = float(ranked.loc[1, "bic"] - ranked.loc[0, "bic"])
print(bic_table.assign(dBIC=bic_table["bic"] - bic_table["bic"].min())
      [["K", "n_parameters", "log_likelihood", "bic", "dBIC", "converged", "smallest_cluster"]]
      .round(1).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nBIC is lowest at K = {K_bic} (at a bound of the range: {K_bic in (PG['k_min'], PG['k_max'])}); "
      f"runner-up K = {k_second}, {bic_margin:,.0f} BIC units worse.")
if not bic_table["converged"].all():
    print("WARNING: EM did not converge for K =", bic_table.loc[~bic_table["converged"], "K"].tolist())

latex.report("clusKMin", PG["k_min"], desc="Smallest K searched")
latex.report("clusKMax", PG["k_max"], desc="Largest K searched")
latex.report("clusNInit", PG["n_init"], desc="EM runs per fit (k-means starts; the best likelihood is kept)")
latex.report("clusKBic", K_bic, desc="Number of clusters with the lowest BIC")
latex.report("clusKSecond", k_second, desc="Second-lowest BIC: its K")
latex.report("clusBicMargin", int(round(bic_margin)), desc="BIC of the second-best K minus the lowest BIC")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-s5-bic
#| fig-cap: "BIC of the mixtures. Left: BIC and AIC for each K (lower is better); the dotted line marks the BIC minimum. Right: BIC relative to its minimum for the K values nearest it."
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.8), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.6, 1]})
ax1.plot(bic_table["K"], bic_table["bic"] / 1e3, "o-", ms=5, lw=2, color=plotting.COLORS["model"], label="BIC")
ax1.plot(bic_table["K"], bic_table["aic"] / 1e3, "s--", ms=4, lw=1.5, color=plotting.COLORS["grey"], label="AIC")
ax1.axvline(K_bic, ls=":", color="black", lw=1)
ax1.set_xticks(k_values)
ax1.set_xlabel("Number of mixture components $K$")
ax1.set_ylabel("Criterion (thousands)")
ax1.legend()
near = bic_table[(bic_table["K"] >= K_bic - 4) & (bic_table["K"] <= K_bic + 3)]
delta_bic = near["bic"] - bic_table["bic"].min()
ax2.bar(near["K"], delta_bic, width=0.7,
        color=[plotting.COLORS["highlight"] if k_ == K_bic else plotting.COLORS["grey"] for k_ in near["K"]])
for k_, v_ in zip(near["K"], delta_bic, strict=True):
    ax2.annotate(f"{v_:,.0f}", (k_, v_), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 3), ha="center", fontsize=8)
ax2.set_xticks(near["K"])
ax2.set_xlabel("$K$")
ax2.set_ylabel("BIC − minimum BIC")
plotting.save_figure(fig, "fig-s5-bic")
plt.show()
```

BIC alone is not a sufficient guide: a partition is worth
describing only if the method gives it again, and it is more useful if it
would also appear in another set of populations.  We check both.

**Reproducibility.**  The likelihood of a mixture has many local maxima,
and EM started from other k-means solutions can end at a different
partition of almost the same likelihood.  For every $K$ the mixture is
refitted from `{python} f"{1 + len(PSt['seeds'])}"` seeds — the chapter's
and those listed under `seeds` in the parameter file, each with
`{python} f"{PG['n_init']}"` EM starts — and the partitions are compared in
pairs with the adjusted Rand index (ARI: 1 = identical, 0 = chance
agreement).  **The chapter uses the largest $K$ whose refits agree at a mean
ARI of at least `{python} f"{PSt['reproducibility_ari']}"`, as do the refits
of every smaller $K$** (`mdmx.clustering.choose_k_reproducible`); its
partition is that $K$'s fit from the sweep above.

```{python}
#| label: c06-reproducibility
#| code-summary: "Refit every K from other seeds and choose K (cached)"
repro_seeds = [PG["seed"], *PSt["seeds"]]


def _reproducibility():
    table, refits = clus.reproducibility_sweep(
        X, k_values, repro_seeds, workers=PSt["workers"],
        **{k_: PG[k_] for k_ in ("covariance_type", "n_init", "max_iter", "tol", "reg_covar")})
    return {"table": table, "labels": {str(k): lab for k, lab in refits.items()}}


repro = artifacts.stage(
    "clustering_reproducibility", _reproducibility, inputs=["tucker", "tensor"],
    params={"features": PF, "gmm": PG, "stability": REPRO_KEY},
    code=[_reproducibility, *FEATURE_CODE, clus.reproducibility_sweep, clus.pairwise_ari, clus._map,
          clus._fit_predict, clus.fit_gmm],
    desc="Refits of the mixture for every K from several seeds, and how far they agree")
repro_table = repro["table"]
K = clus.choose_k_reproducible(repro_table, PSt["reproducibility_ari"])
chosen = fit["fits"][str(K)]
labels = chosen["labels"]
# The refit from the chapter's own seed (first row) must give, up to the agreement the rule asks
# of the refits, the chapter's partition; otherwise the agreement measured above would not be
# the chapter partition's.
own_refit_ari = adjusted_rand_score(labels, repro["labels"][str(K)][0])
if own_refit_ari < PSt["reproducibility_ari"]:
    raise ValueError(f"The refit of K = {K} from the chapter's seed differs from the chapter's fit "
                     f"(ARI {own_refit_ari:.3f}).")
ari_at = dict(zip(repro_table["K"], repro_table["ari_mean"], strict=True))
ari_next = ari_at.get(K + 1)
sizes = np.bincount(labels, minlength=K)
uncertain = float(np.mean(chosen["posterior"].max(axis=1) < PD["posterior_cut"]))
latex.report("clusPosteriorCut", f"{PD['posterior_cut']:g}",
             desc="Largest posterior probability below which an assignment counts as uncertain")
print(repro_table.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nChosen K = {K}: the largest K whose refits agree at mean ARI ≥ {PSt['reproducibility_ari']}, "
      f"as do those of every smaller K (BIC's K = {K_bic}).")
print(f"The chapter's fit against its refit from the same seed: ARI {own_refit_ari:.3f}")
print("Cluster sizes:", sizes.tolist())
print(f"Country-years whose largest posterior probability is below 0.9: {100 * uncertain:.1f}%")
if K > len(plotting.CLUSTER_COLORS):
    raise ValueError(f"K = {K} exceeds the {len(plotting.CLUSTER_COLORS)} cluster colours in mdmx.plotting.")
CL = list(plotting.CLUSTER_COLORS[:K])
CNAME = [f"Cluster {k + 1}" for k in range(K)]

latex.report("clusK", K, desc="Number of clusters: the largest K whose refits from other seeds agree")
latex.report("clusReproThreshold", PSt["reproducibility_ari"], digits=2,
             desc="Smallest mean pairwise ARI between refits for a K to count as reproducible")
latex.report("clusNReproFits", len(repro_seeds), desc="Refits per K compared for reproducibility")
latex.report("clusReproAri", float(ari_at[K]), digits=2, desc="Mean pairwise ARI between the refits at the chosen K")
if ari_next is not None:
    latex.report("clusReproAriNext", float(ari_next), digits=2,
                 desc="Mean pairwise ARI between the refits at the chosen K plus one")
latex.report("clusReproAriBic", float(ari_at[K_bic]), digits=2,
             desc="Mean pairwise ARI between the refits at BIC's K")
# The rule keeps K for every threshold above the agreement at K + 1 and up to the lowest agreement up to K.
_ari_floor = float(min(ari_at[k_] for k_ in k_values if k_ <= K))
# Printed rounded down: every threshold up to the printed value keeps K (0.977 rounded to 0.98 would not).
latex.report("clusReproAriFloor", _ari_floor, digits=2, text=f"{np.floor(100 * _ari_floor) / 100:.2f}",
             desc="Lowest mean pairwise ARI between the refits over K up to the chosen K (rounded down)")
latex.report("clusBicAboveMin", int(round(bic_at[K] - bic_at[K_bic])),
             desc="BIC of the chosen K minus the lowest BIC")
for k in range(K):
    latex.report(f"clusSize{WORDS[k]}", int(sizes[k]), desc=f"Country-years in cluster {k + 1}")
latex.report("clusSizes", int(sizes.sum()),
             text=", ".join(latex.fmt_int(s) for s in sizes[:-1]) + " and " + latex.fmt_int(sizes[-1]),
             desc="Cluster sizes, in cluster order, as a list")
latex.report("clusSizeMin", int(sizes.min()), desc="Smallest cluster size")
latex.report("clusSizeMax", int(sizes.max()), desc="Largest cluster size")
latex.report("clusShareUncertain", 100 * uncertain, digits=1,
             desc="Percent of country-years with largest posterior probability below 0.9")
```

**Resampling of populations.**  Reproducibility is a property of the
method on these data.  Whether the clusters would also appear in another
set of populations is a different question.  Following @Hennig2007, we
resample whole *population families* — a population together with its HMD
parts, such as the United Kingdom with England & Wales, Scotland and
Northern Ireland (`svdcomp.population_families`), because the years of one
population are not independent — with replacement, refit the mixture to
each of `{python} f"{PSt['bootstrap_resamples']}"` resamples
(each with the `{python} f"{PG['n_init']}"` EM starts of the chapter's
partition, so that the check measures the populations and not the
starting values), and record for
every cluster its Jaccard similarity with its best match in the refit, on
the country-years in the resample (`mdmx.clustering.group_bootstrap`,
`cluster_jaccard`).  A cluster's mean Jaccard is read as in Hennig's
`fpc::clusterboot`: at least `{python} f"{PSt['jaccard_stable']}"` a stable
cluster, from `{python} f"{PSt['jaccard_doubtful']}"` a pattern whose
members are doubtful, below that a cluster not to be trusted.  The check is
reported for every $K$; it does not choose $K$.

```{python}
#| label: c06-bootstrap
#| code-summary: "Resample population families and refit every K (cached)"
family = sc.population_families(pops, artifacts.load("populations"))[c_idx]   # (n_obs,)
boot_settings = {k_: PG[k_] for k_ in ("covariance_type", "max_iter", "tol", "reg_covar")}


def _bootstrap():
    return {str(k): clus.group_bootstrap(X, fit["fits"][str(k)]["labels"], family, k,
                                         n_resamples=PSt["bootstrap_resamples"], seed=PSt["bootstrap_seed"],
                                         n_init=PG["n_init"], workers=PSt["workers"], **boot_settings)
            for k in k_values}


boot = artifacts.stage(
    "clustering_bootstrap", _bootstrap, inputs=["tucker", "tensor", "populations", "clustering_gmm"],
    params={"features": PF, "gmm": PG, "stability": BOOT_KEY},
    code=[_bootstrap, *FEATURE_CODE, sc.population_families, clus.group_bootstrap, clus.group_resample,
          clus.cluster_jaccard, clus._map, clus._fit_predict, clus.fit_gmm],
    desc="Refits of the mixture to resamples of whole population families, for every K")


boot_by_k = clus.bootstrap_summary({int(k): res for k, res in boot.items()})
jac_K, present_K = clus.cluster_stability(boot[str(K)], K)   # (K,) mean Jaccard, resamples holding the cluster
n_families = int(np.unique(family).size)
boot_ari_K = float(boot_by_k.set_index("K").loc[K, "ari"])
print(boot_by_k.merge(repro_table, on="K").round(3).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nPopulation families: {n_families}.  At K = {K}, mean Jaccard by cluster: {np.round(jac_K, 2).tolist()} "
      f"(resamples holding the cluster: {present_K.tolist()} of {PSt['bootstrap_resamples']})")

latex.report("clusNBoot", PSt["bootstrap_resamples"], desc="Resamples of population families")
latex.report("clusNFamilies", n_families, desc="Population families resampled")
latex.report("clusJaccardStable", PSt["jaccard_stable"], digits=2, desc="Mean Jaccard of a stable cluster (Hennig)")
latex.report("clusJaccardDoubtful", PSt["jaccard_doubtful"], digits=2,
             desc="Mean Jaccard below which a cluster is not to be trusted (Hennig)")
latex.report("clusNJaccardBelowDoubtful", int(np.sum(jac_K < PSt["jaccard_doubtful"])),
             desc="Clusters at the chosen K whose mean Jaccard is below the not-to-be-trusted threshold")
latex.report("clusJaccardMin", float(jac_K.min()), digits=2,
             desc="Smallest mean Jaccard of a cluster at the chosen K (resampling population families)")
latex.report("clusJaccardMax", float(jac_K.max()), digits=2,
             desc="Largest mean Jaccard of a cluster at the chosen K (resampling population families)")
latex.report("clusBootAri", boot_ari_K, digits=2,
             desc="Mean ARI between the chosen partition and the refits to resampled population families")
latex.report("clusKJaccardBest", int(boot_by_k.loc[boot_by_k["jaccard_min"].idxmax(), "K"]),
             desc="K whose least stable cluster has the largest mean Jaccard (resampling population families)")
latex.report("clusJaccardBestMin", float(boot_by_k["jaccard_min"].max()), digits=2,
             desc="Largest, over K, of the smallest mean Jaccard of a cluster")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-s5-stability
#| fig-cap: "The choice of K. Left: agreement between refits of the mixture from different starting values (adjusted Rand index; mean and smallest over pairs); the chosen K (shaded) is the largest K up to which the mean meets the threshold (dashed). Middle: stability of the clusters when whole population families are resampled — each cluster's mean Jaccard similarity with its best match, for the least stable cluster and averaged over the clusters; dotted lines at Hennig's thresholds for a doubtful and a stable cluster. Right: BIC relative to its minimum."
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.6), sharex=True)
for ax in axes:
    ax.axvspan(K - 0.4, K + 0.4, color=plotting.COLORS["highlight"], alpha=0.25, lw=0, zorder=0)
    ax.set_xticks(k_values)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=8)
    ax.set_xlabel("$K$")
ax = axes[0]
ax.plot(repro_table["K"], repro_table["ari_mean"], "o-", ms=4, lw=2, color=plotting.COLORS["model"], label="Mean")
ax.plot(repro_table["K"], repro_table["ari_min"], "o--", ms=3, lw=1.2, color=plotting.COLORS["grey"],
        label="Smallest pair")
ax.axhline(PSt["reproducibility_ari"], ls="--", color="black", lw=0.8)
ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.05)
ax.set_ylabel("ARI between refits")
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower left")
ax = axes[1]
ax.plot(boot_by_k["K"], boot_by_k["jaccard_mean"], "o-", ms=4, lw=2, color=plotting.COLORS["model"],
        label="Average over clusters")
ax.plot(boot_by_k["K"], boot_by_k["jaccard_min"], "o--", ms=3, lw=1.2, color=plotting.COLORS["grey"],
        label="Least stable cluster")
for threshold in (PSt["jaccard_doubtful"], PSt["jaccard_stable"]):
    ax.axhline(threshold, ls=":", color="black", lw=0.8)
ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.05)
ax.set_ylabel("Mean Jaccard (resampled families)")
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower left")
ax = axes[2]
ax.plot(bic_table["K"], (bic_table["bic"] - bic_table["bic"].min()) / 1e3, "o-", ms=4, lw=2,
        color=plotting.COLORS["grey"])
ax.set_ylabel("BIC − minimum (thousands)")
fig.tight_layout()
plotting.save_figure(fig, "fig-s5-stability")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: c06-k-text
#| output: asis
#| code-summary: "Text: what the choice of K and the resampling check show"
stable_k = boot_by_k.loc[boot_by_k["jaccard_min"] >= PSt["jaccard_stable"], "K"].tolist()
best_row = boot_by_k.loc[boot_by_k["jaccard_min"].idxmax()]
n_untrusted = int(np.sum(jac_K < PSt["jaccard_doubtful"]))
thr = PSt["reproducibility_ari"]
# Agreement need not fall monotonically with K; say what happens above K + 1 too.
above = [k for k in k_values if k > K + 1]
again = [k for k in above if ari_at[k] >= thr]
rest = [ari_at[k] for k in above if k not in again]
after = ""
if ari_next is not None:
    after = f"; at $K$ = {K + 1} they agree only at {ari_next:.2f}"
if again:
    after += (f", $K$ = {' and '.join(str(k) for k in again)} {'reach' if len(again) > 1 else 'reaches'} "
              f"{thr} again ({', '.join(f'{ari_at[k]:.2f}' for k in again)})")
if rest:
    after += f", and no other $K$ does (at most {max(rest):.2f})"
# The thresholds that give the same K: above the agreement at K + 1, up to the lowest agreement up to K.
low, high = (ari_next if ari_next is not None else 0.0), min(ari_at[k] for k in k_values if k <= K)
print(f"BIC is lowest at $K$ = {K_bic}"
      f"{' (the upper bound of the range)' if K_bic == PG['k_max'] else ''}, but the refits from other "
      f"starting values agree at a mean ARI of at least {thr} only up to $K$ = {K} ({ari_at[K]:.2f}{after}).  "
      "A partition that another seed would change is not worth describing, so the rule stops at the first "
      f"$K$ whose refits disagree; any threshold above {low:.2f} and up to {high:.2f} gives the same $K$.  "
      f"The chapter therefore uses $K$ = {K} clusters, {bic_at[K] - bic_at[K_bic]:,.0f} BIC units above "
      f"the minimum.  Cluster sizes range from {sizes.min():,} to {sizes.max():,} country-years, and "
      f"{100 * uncertain:.0f}% of country-years have a largest posterior probability below 0.9.\n")
if stable_k:
    stable_text = (f"Only $K$ = {', '.join(str(k) for k in stable_k)} keep every cluster stable "
                   f"(mean Jaccard ≥ {PSt['jaccard_stable']}) when whole population families are resampled.")
else:
    stable_text = (f"When whole population families are resampled, no $K$ keeps every cluster stable (mean "
                   f"Jaccard ≥ {PSt['jaccard_stable']}); the best is $K$ = {int(best_row['K'])}, whose least "
                   f"stable cluster reaches {best_row['jaccard_min']:.2f}.")
print(f"{stable_text}  At $K$ = {K} the clusters' mean Jaccard similarities range from {jac_K.min():.2f} to "
      f"{jac_K.max():.2f} ({n_untrusted} of {K} below {PSt['jaccard_doubtful']}), and the refits agree with "
      f"the chapter's partition at a mean ARI of {boot_ari_K:.2f}, against {ari_at[K]:.2f} for refits to all "
      "populations from other starting values: most of the instability comes from which populations are in "
      "the sample — a cluster made up mostly of a few populations cannot form in a resample without them.  "
      "If anything the check is lenient, because the typical schedule (Step 3) and the PCA are fitted to "
      "all populations and held fixed; only the mixture is refitted.  The clusters are a reproducible "
      f"description of these {C} populations — a typology in the spirit of the regional model life tables "
      "of @CoaleDemeny1966 — not regimes that any set of populations would reproduce.\n")
```

## Step 6 — Ward's hierarchical clustering as a check

This check, which is in the companion only, compares the mixture with Ward's
minimum-variance clustering on the same reduced features.  The tree is built on all
`{python} f"{n_obs:,}"` country-years, cut into $K$ groups, and matched to the
mixture clusters to maximise agreement (`matched_agreement`); we report the
share of country-years on which they agree and the adjusted Rand index
(ARI: 0 for chance, 1 for identical partitions).

```{python}
#| label: c06-ward
#| code-summary: "Ward's method on the same features, and its agreement with the mixture"
Z_ward, ward_raw = clus.ward_clustering(X, K)
ward_agree, ward_conf, ward_map = clus.matched_agreement(ward_raw, labels, K)
ward_labels = ward_map[ward_raw]
ward_ari = adjusted_rand_score(labels, ward_raw)
print(f"Ward vs mixture: matched agreement {ward_agree:.3f}, ARI {ward_ari:.3f}")
latex.report("clusWardAgree", 100 * ward_agree, digits=0, desc="Percent of country-years on which Ward and GMM agree (matched labels)")
latex.report("clusWardARI", float(ward_ari), digits=2, desc="Adjusted Rand index between Ward and GMM partitions")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-s5-dendrogram
#| fig-cap: "Ward's dendrogram of the reduced level-free features, truncated to its last merges. Branch colours show the mixture cluster holding most country-years below each branch; the bars underneath show the full mixture composition of each truncated leaf. The dashed line is the cut that gives K groups."
node_counts = clus.node_label_counts(Z_ward, labels, K)
node_major = node_counts.argmax(axis=1)
fig, (ax, axb) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(11, 5.2), sharex=True,
                              gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [4, 1], "hspace": 0.05})
dd = dendrogram(Z_ward, truncate_mode="lastp", p=PD["dendrogram_leaves"], no_labels=True, ax=ax,
                link_color_func=lambda node: CL[node_major[node]])
ax.axhline((Z_ward[-K, 2] + Z_ward[-K + 1, 2]) / 2, ls="--", color="black", lw=0.8)
ax.set_ylabel("Ward linkage distance")
ax.grid(False)
leaf_ids = np.asarray(dd["leaves"])
comp = node_counts[leaf_ids] / node_counts[leaf_ids].sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
leaf_x = 5 + 10 * np.arange(len(leaf_ids))            # scipy places leaves at 5, 15, 25, …
bottom = np.zeros(len(leaf_ids))
for k in range(K):
    axb.bar(leaf_x, comp[:, k], bottom=bottom, width=9, color=CL[k], edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.3)
    bottom += comp[:, k]
axb.set_ylim(0, 1)
axb.set_ylabel("Mixture\nshare", fontsize=8)
axb.set_xlabel(f"Truncated leaves (last {PD['dendrogram_leaves']} merges), ordered as in the tree")
axb.grid(False)
fig.legend(handles=[Patch(color=CL[k], label=str(k + 1)) for k in range(K)], loc="upper center",
           ncol=K, title="Cluster", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.02), fontsize=8)
plotting.save_figure(fig, "fig-s5-dendrogram")
plt.show()
```

Ward and the mixture agree on `{python} f"{100 * ward_agree:.0f}"`% of
country-years after matching (ARI `{python} f"{ward_ari:.2f}"`).  The two
methods answer different questions — Ward minimises Euclidean within-group
spread, the mixture also models each cluster's own covariance — so their
agreement is only partial.

## Step 7 — what the clusters are

Each cluster is summarised by its **mean deviation** $\bar{\mathbf{f}}_k$, the
mean of its members' features (`mdmx.clustering.cluster_means`).  Mapped
back to core coordinates (`features_to_cores`: the feature entries filled
in, zeros elsewhere) it is a matrix $\mathbf{D}_k$, and the cluster's
schedule at any life expectancy $x$ is

$$
\mathcal{M}_k(x) \;=\; \mathbf{S}\,\bigl[\bar{\mathcal{G}}(x) + \mathbf{D}_k\bigr]\,\mathbf{A}^\top,
$$

the typical schedule at $x$ plus the cluster's deviation
$\mathbf{S}\mathbf{D}_k\mathbf{A}^\top$, which is the same at every $x$.
The members' own schedules, and their e₀, vary widely within a cluster;
what they share is the deviation.

```{python}
#| label: c06-centroids
#| code-summary: "Cluster deviations, and the noise and population-size measures"
residual_mean = clus.cluster_means(R, labels, K)                              # (K, p)
residual_core = clus.features_to_cores(residual_mean, fidx, r1, r2)          # (K, r1, r2)
deviation = tz.schedules_from_cores(np.moveaxis(residual_core, 0, -1), U_sex, U_age)   # (S, A, K)
member_mean_core = clus.cluster_means(G_obs, labels, K)                       # (K, r1, r2)

# Noise measures (Step 8): roughness of each observed schedule relative to the
# typical roughness at the same e0, and population size (total HMD exposure).
rough = clus.roughness(T["M"], c_idx, t_idx, *PX["noise_ages"])
log_rough = np.log10(rough)
log_rough_fit, _ = clus.conditional_mean(e0, log_rough, **cm)
excess_rough = log_rough - log_rough_fit
exposure = hmd["de"].groupby(["pop", "year"])["exposure"].sum()
size = exposure.reindex(pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays([pops[c_idx], obs_year])).to_numpy()
if np.isnan(size).any():
    raise ValueError("Some observed country-years have no HMD exposures.")
log_size = np.log10(size)
small = log_size <= np.quantile(log_size, 0.25)
noise_tab = clus.noise_diagnostics(labels, K, excess_rough, small,
                                   roughness_ratio=PX["noise_roughness_ratio"],
                                   small_share=PX["noise_small_share"])
noise_clusters = np.flatnonzero(noise_tab["noise"].to_numpy())

# Mean deviation in logit(q_x) by broad age group, for describing the clusters.
AGE_GROUPS = {"0": (0, 1), "1–14": (1, 15), "15–34": (15, 35), "35–64": (35, 65), "65–89": (65, 90)}
dev_tab = pd.DataFrame({f"{SEXES[s][0]} {g}": deviation[s, a:b].mean(axis=0)
                        for s in range(2) for g, (a, b) in AGE_GROUPS.items()},
                       index=pd.Index(np.arange(1, K + 1), name="Cluster"))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-s5-cluster-summary
#| code-summary: "Table: one row per cluster"
rows = []
for k in range(K):
    m = labels == k
    member_pops = pd.Series(pops[c_idx[m]]).value_counts()
    rows.append({
        "Cluster": k + 1,
        "Country-years": int(m.sum()),
        "Populations": int(member_pops.size),
        "Years": f"{obs_year[m].min()}--{obs_year[m].max()}",
        "Median year": int(np.median(obs_year[m])),
        r"$e_0$ mean (SD)": f"{e0[m].mean():.1f} ({e0[m].std():.1f})",
        r"$e_0$ range": f"{e0[m].min():.1f}--{e0[m].max():.1f}",
        "Roughness ratio": float(noise_tab.loc[k, "roughness_ratio"]),
        "Jaccard": float(jac_K[k]),
        "Largest contributors": ", ".join(member_pops.index[:3]),
    })
summary = pd.DataFrame(rows)
# For the article the table is transposed (the table standard: more columns than rows): one column per
# cluster, the attributes as rows, every cell formatted here.
summary_tex = pd.DataFrame({
    f"Cluster {r['Cluster']}": [latex.fmt_int(r["Country-years"]), str(r["Populations"]), r["Years"],
                                str(r["Median year"]), r["$e_0$ mean (SD)"], r["$e_0$ range"],
                                f"{r['Roughness ratio']:.2f}", f"{r['Jaccard']:.2f}",
                                "\\makecell[r]{" + "\\\\".join(latex.latex_escape(c) for c in
                                                                r["Largest contributors"].split(", ")) + "}"]
    for r in rows})
summary_tex.insert(0, "", ["Country-years", "Populations", "Years", "Median year", "$e_0$ mean (SD)", "$e_0$ range",
                           "Roughness ratio", "Jaccard", "Largest contributors"])
latex.save_table(
    summary_tex, "tbl-s5-cluster-summary",
    "The level-free clusters.  $e_0$ is that of the observed schedule (mean of the sexes).  "
    "\\emph{Roughness ratio}: median roughness of the members' observed schedules relative to "
    "typical schedules with the same $e_0$ (1 = typical).  \\emph{Jaccard}: the cluster's mean "
    "Jaccard similarity with its best match when the mixture is refitted to resamples of whole "
    f"population families (1 = always recovered; Hennig's reading: at least {PSt['jaccard_stable']} "
    f"stable, below {PSt['jaccard_doubtful']} not to be trusted).  "
    "\\emph{Largest contributors}: the three populations with the most country-years in the cluster.",
    short_caption="The level-free clusters", column_format="l" + "r" * len(rows), escape_cells=False)
summary
```

### The clusters in words

The description below is generated from the table of mean deviations: an
age group is mentioned when a cluster's mean deviation there is at least
`{python} f"{PD['describe_threshold']}"` in logit units (about 16% higher or
lower odds of dying than typical at the same e₀).

```{python}
#| label: c06-describe
#| output: asis
#| code-summary: "Describe each cluster from its deviation pattern and members"
thr = PD["describe_threshold"]
SEX_WORD = {"F": "female", "M": "male"}

def _groups(cols):
    """'F 1–14', 'M 0' → 'female 1–14, male 0'."""
    return ", ".join(f"{SEX_WORD[c_.split()[0]]} {c_.split()[1]}" for c_ in cols)

near_zero = [k for k in range(K) if np.abs(dev_tab.loc[k + 1]).max() < thr]
latex.report("clusDescribeThreshold", thr, digits=2,
             desc="Mean deviation (logit) from which an age group is named in a cluster's description")
if near_zero:
    which = " and ".join([", ".join(str(k + 1) for k in near_zero[:-1]), str(near_zero[-1] + 1)]) \
        if len(near_zero) > 1 else str(near_zero[0] + 1)
    many = len(near_zero) > 1
    near_text = (f"Cluster{'s' if many else ''} {which} {'have' if many else 'has'} a mean deviation close "
                 f"to zero in every age group: {'they are' if many else 'it is'} distinguished from the rest by "
                 "how widely and in which directions the members scatter around the typical schedule, not by "
                 f"a shift away from it, and {'their' if many else 'its'} schedule at any e₀ is essentially "
                 "the typical one.")
else:
    near_text = "Every cluster departs from the typical schedule in at least one age group."
for k in range(K):
    m = labels == k
    top = ", ".join(NAME[p_] for p_ in pd.Series(pops[c_idx[m]]).value_counts().index[:3])
    hi = [c_ for c_ in dev_tab.columns if dev_tab.loc[k + 1, c_] >= thr]
    lo = [c_ for c_ in dev_tab.columns if dev_tab.loc[k + 1, c_] <= -thr]
    if hi or lo:
        parts = ([f"higher than typical at {_groups(hi)}"] if hi else []) + \
                ([f"lower at {_groups(lo)}"] if lo else [])
        shape = "mortality " + "; ".join(parts)
    else:
        shape = f"within ±{thr} of the typical schedule in every age group"
    flag = " **Flagged as a small-population noise cluster (Step 8).**" if k in noise_clusters else ""
    print(f"* **Cluster {k + 1}** ({sizes[k]:,} country-years; mean e₀ {e0[m].mean():.1f}; "
          f"median year {int(np.median(obs_year[m]))}; mostly {top}): {shape}.{flag}")
print()
```

The spaghetti plots show, for each cluster, the deviations of individual

```{python}
    """One row per cluster, females left and males right."""
```

## Step 8 — level, time, and noise

**Level and time.**  The features have no mean dependence on e₀, but the
clusters can still differ in e₀ if different groups of populations are
observed at different levels of mortality — below e₀ = 40 only a handful of
populations are in the HMD.  The correlation ratio $\eta^2$ (the share of a
variable's variance explained by cluster membership;
`mdmx.clustering.eta_squared`) measures this for e₀ and for calendar year;
the number of clusters present at each level of e₀ shows whether the
clusters are level strata.

```{python}
#| label: c06-level
#| code-summary: "How much of e0 and calendar time the clusters explain"
eta_e0 = clus.eta_squared(e0, labels)
eta_year = clus.eta_squared(obs_year.astype(float), labels)
e0_band = pd.cut(e0, np.arange(15, 95, PD["e0_bin"]))
per_band = pd.crosstab(e0_band, labels)
clusters_per_band = (per_band >= PD["band_min_members"]).sum(axis=1)
well_filled = per_band.sum(axis=1) >= PD["band_min_obs"]
latex.report("clusBandMinObs", PD["band_min_obs"], desc="Observed country-years for an e0 band to count as well filled")
mid_bands = clusters_per_band[[(iv.left >= 65) and (iv.right <= 80) for iv in clusters_per_band.index]]
if mid_bands.min() == K:
    mid_band_text = f"all {K}"
elif mid_bands.min() == mid_bands.max():
    mid_band_text = f"{int(mid_bands.min())} of the {K}"
else:
    mid_band_text = f"{int(mid_bands.min())}–{int(mid_bands.max())} of the {K}"
print(f"eta² of e0 on the clusters:   {eta_e0:.3f}")
print(f"eta² of year on the clusters: {eta_year:.3f}")
print(f"Clusters with ≥ {PD['band_min_members']} members in each {PD['e0_bin']}-year e0 band:")
print(pd.DataFrame({"country-years": per_band.sum(axis=1), "clusters present": clusters_per_band}).to_string())
latex.report("clusEtaEzero", float(eta_e0), digits=2, desc="Share of e0 variance explained by cluster (eta squared)")
latex.report("clusEtaYear", float(eta_year), digits=2, desc="Share of calendar-year variance explained by cluster (eta squared)")
latex.report("clusMinClustersPerBand", int(clusters_per_band[well_filled].min()),
             desc="Fewest clusters present in an e0 band with at least 100 country-years")
latex.report("clusBandMinMembers", PD["band_min_members"],
             desc="Members a cluster needs in an e0 band to count as present there")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-s5-geography
#| fig-cap: "Composition of the clusters. Top: share of each population's observed country-years in each cluster (populations sorted by their majority cluster, then by its share). Bottom: calendar years (left) and e₀ of the observed schedules (right) of the members of each cluster (boxes: quartiles; whiskers: 5th and 95th percentiles)."
counts_ck = clus.label_counts(labels, c_idx, C, K)                # (C, K)
frac_ck = counts_ck / counts_ck.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
major_c = clus.majority_label(labels, c_idx, C, K)
order_c = np.lexsort((-frac_ck.max(axis=1), major_c))
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8.5))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, height_ratios=[1.1, 1], hspace=0.6, wspace=0.2)
ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :])
bottom = np.zeros(C)
for k in range(K):
    ax.bar(np.arange(C), frac_ck[order_c, k], bottom=bottom, color=CL[k], width=0.85,
           edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.3, label=str(k + 1))
    bottom += frac_ck[order_c, k]
ax.set_xticks(np.arange(C), names[order_c], rotation=90, fontsize=7)
ax.set_xlim(-0.6, C - 0.4)
ax.set_ylabel("Share of country-years")
ax.legend(ncol=K, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.2), title="Cluster", fontsize=8)
ax.grid(False)
for pos, (vals, lab) in enumerate([(obs_year, "Year"), (e0, "$e_0$ of the observed schedule (years)")]):
    axb = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, pos])
    bp = axb.boxplot([vals[labels == k] for k in range(K)], whis=(5, 95), showfliers=False,
                     patch_artist=True, widths=0.6)
    for k, box in enumerate(bp["boxes"]):
        box.set_facecolor(CL[k])
        box.set_alpha(0.8)
    for med in bp["medians"]:
        med.set_color("black")
    axb.set_xticks(np.arange(1, K + 1), [str(k + 1) for k in range(K)])
    axb.set_xlabel("Cluster")
    axb.set_ylabel(lab)
plotting.save_figure(fig, "fig-s5-geography")
plt.show()
```

Where the data allow a test, the clusters are not level strata: every
5-year e₀ band with at least 100 country-years contains at least
`{python} f"{int(clusters_per_band[well_filled].min())}"` clusters, and the
bands between e₀ = 65 and 80 contain `{python} mid_band_text`.  Cluster
membership explains $\eta^2$ = `{python} f"{eta_e0:.2f}"` of the variance
of e₀ and $\eta^2$ = `{python} f"{eta_year:.2f}"` of the variance of
calendar year.  This is not level leaking back into the features, whose
mean does not depend on e₀ (Step 3).  What association there is comes from
composition — below e₀ ≈ 45 only a few populations with long early series
are observed, so the deviation patterns found there are theirs, and
populations that enter the HMD late are observed only at high e₀ — and from
spread: the residuals are larger at high mortality, and clusters that
differ mainly in how widely their members scatter (see Step 7) differ in
e₀ and period with it.  The clusters are therefore free of level in the
sense intended — they are defined by deviations from the typical schedule
at the same e₀ — but they are not uncorrelated with level or period.

**Noise.**  A cluster can form around the noisy schedules of small
populations, above all when the features include the high-order age
columns (Step 2).  We check every cluster with two
measures: the **roughness ratio** — the median roughness of its members'
observed schedules (mean squared second difference of logit $q_x$ over ages
`{python} f"{PX['noise_ages'][0]}"`–`{python} f"{PX['noise_ages'][1]}"`,
`mdmx.clustering.roughness`) relative to typical schedules at the same e₀
(a LOWESS of log roughness on e₀) — and the **share of its members from
the smallest quarter of country-years by population size** (total HMD
exposure).  A cluster is flagged as a noise cluster if its roughness ratio
exceeds `{python} f"{PX['noise_roughness_ratio']}"` *and* more than
`{python} f"{PX['noise_small_share']:.0%}"` of its members come from the
smallest quarter (`mdmx.clustering.noise_diagnostics`).

```{python}
#| label: c06-noise
#| code-summary: "Noise diagnostics for every cluster"
low_mort = e0 > np.median(e0)
eta_rough_low = clus.eta_squared(excess_rough[low_mort], labels[low_mort])
eta_size_low = clus.eta_squared(log_size[low_mort], labels[low_mort])
print(noise_tab.assign(cluster=noise_tab["cluster"] + 1).round(2).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nFlagged noise clusters: {[int(k) + 1 for k in noise_clusters] or 'none'} "
      f"({int(sizes[noise_clusters].sum())} country-years)")
print(f"eta² on the clusters, country-years with e0 above the median: excess roughness {eta_rough_low:.2f}, "
      f"log population size {eta_size_low:.2f}")
latex.report("clusNNoise", int(len(noise_clusters)), desc="Number of clusters flagged as small-population noise clusters")
latex.report("clusNoiseMembers", int(sizes[noise_clusters].sum()), desc="Country-years in flagged noise clusters")
latex.report("clusNoiseRatioMax", float(noise_tab["roughness_ratio"].max()), digits=1,
             desc="Largest roughness ratio of a cluster")
latex.report("clusNoiseRatioThreshold", PX["noise_roughness_ratio"], digits=1,
             desc="Roughness ratio above which a cluster can be flagged as a noise cluster")
latex.report("clusNoiseSmallThreshold", 100 * PX["noise_small_share"], digits=0,
             desc="Percent of members from the smallest quarter by size above which a cluster can be flagged")
# The text describes one noise cluster; with none or several there is no single share to quote.
if len(noise_clusters) == 1:
    latex.report("clusNoiseSmallShare", 100 * float(noise_tab.loc[noise_clusters[0], "small_share"]), digits=0,
                 desc="Percent of the noise cluster's members from the smallest quarter of country-years by size")
else:
    print(f"clusNoiseSmallShare not reported: {len(noise_clusters)} noise clusters, and the text describes one.")
latex.report("clusEtaRough", float(eta_rough_low), digits=2,
             desc="eta squared of excess log roughness on clusters, e0 above median")
latex.report("clusEtaSize", float(eta_size_low), digits=2,
             desc="eta squared of log population size on clusters, e0 above median")
```

```{python}
#| label: c06-noise-text
#| output: asis
#| code-summary: "Text: what the noise check found"
if len(noise_clusters) == 0:
    print("No cluster meets the noise rule.")
else:
    for k in noise_clusters:
        m = labels == k
        top = ", ".join(NAME[p_] for p_ in pd.Series(pops[c_idx[m]]).value_counts().index[:3])
        print(f"Cluster {k + 1} meets the noise rule: its members' schedules are "
              f"{noise_tab.loc[k, 'roughness_ratio']:.1f} times as rough as typical schedules at the "
              f"same e₀, and {100 * noise_tab.loc[k, 'small_share']:.0f}% of its {sizes[k]} members come "
              f"from the smallest quarter of country-years by population size (mostly {top}). ")
    print(f"It holds {100 * sizes[noise_clusters].sum() / n_obs:.1f}% of the observed country-years; "
          "it is reported here, and later chapters exclude it through the artefact's `noise_clusters` "
          "entry. ")
others = noise_tab[~noise_tab["noise"]]
print(f"The other clusters have roughness ratios between {others['roughness_ratio'].min():.2f} and "
      f"{others['roughness_ratio'].max():.2f}, and at most {100 * others['small_share'].max():.0f}% of the "
      f"members of any of them come from the smallest quarter of country-years by size (against "
      f"{100 * small.mean():.0f}% of all country-years). ")
print(f"Among country-years with e₀ above the median, cluster membership still explains "
      f"$\\eta^2$ = {eta_rough_low:.2f} of excess roughness and {eta_size_low:.2f} of log population "
      "size: data quality remains one of the things the partition reflects.")
```

## Step 9 — countries, regions and periods

### Majority labels

Two derived clusterings, in the companion only, summarise the country-year labels: a
population's **country cluster** is the cluster of the majority of its observed
country-years, and a year's **year cluster** is the cluster of the majority of
populations observed that year.  Both come from `mdmx.clustering.majority_label`, the
single implementation of every majority vote in this chapter: only observed
country-years vote, a population or year with none gets no label (`-1`),
and **ties go to the lower-numbered cluster**.

```{python}
#| label: c06-derived
#| code-summary: "Country and year clusters by majority vote; stability within countries"
country_cluster = clus.majority_label(labels, c_idx, C, K)          # (C,)
year_cluster = clus.majority_label(labels, t_idx, Tn, K)            # (T,), -1 where no data
purity = counts_ck.max(axis=1) / counts_ck.sum(axis=1)
n_multi = int(np.sum((counts_ck > 0).sum(axis=1) > 1))
switches = clus.switch_share(labels, c_idx)
n_country_ties = int(np.sum((counts_ck == counts_ck.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)).sum(axis=1) > 1))
print("Populations per country cluster:", np.bincount(country_cluster, minlength=K).tolist())
print(f"Populations with country-years in more than one cluster: {n_multi} of {C}")
print(f"Median share of a population's country-years in its majority cluster: {np.median(purity):.2f}")
print(f"Consecutive observed years of a population in different clusters: {100 * switches:.1f}%")
print(f"Populations whose country cluster was decided by the tie-break: {n_country_ties}")
latex.report("clusNPopsMulti", n_multi, desc="Populations with country-years in more than one cluster")
latex.report("clusSwitchShare", 100 * switches, digits=1,
             desc="Percent of consecutive observed years of a population that change cluster")
latex.report("clusMedianPurity", 100 * float(np.median(purity)), digits=0,
             desc="Median percent of a population's country-years in its majority cluster")
```

### Regions

The regional grouping is listed in the parameter file, and
`mdmx.clustering.region_of` stops with an error if a population is missing
or listed twice.  Aggregates and their parts (for
example the United Kingdom and England & Wales) are both clustered, so both
are counted.

```{python}
#| label: fig-s5-region-summary
#| fig-cap: "Country-years of each region by cluster. Aggregate populations and their parts (e.g. United Kingdom and England & Wales) are both counted, because both are clustered."
region = clus.region_of(pops, REGIONS)
region_names = list(REGIONS)
region_idx = np.array([region_names.index(r) for r in region[c_idx]])
counts_rk = clus.label_counts(labels, region_idx, len(region_names), K)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.5))
left = np.zeros(len(region_names))
ypos = np.arange(len(region_names))[::-1]
for k in range(K):
    ax.barh(ypos, counts_rk[:, k], left=left, color=CL[k], edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.8,
            height=0.75, label=str(k + 1))
    left += counts_rk[:, k]
ax.set_yticks(ypos, region_names)
ax.set_xlabel("Observed country-years")
ax.legend(loc="lower right", ncol=3, title="Cluster", fontsize=8)
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
plotting.save_figure(fig, "fig-s5-region-summary")
plt.show()
```

Because level has been removed, the paths do not run along an axis of
mortality decline: the leading principal components are nearly
uncorrelated with e₀ (largest |r| =
`{python} f"{pc_corr['corr with e0'].abs().max():.2f}"`).  Populations
wander within the cloud of deviation patterns:
`{python} f"{n_multi}"` of `{python} f"{C}"` populations pass through more
than one cluster, a median of
`{python} f"{100 * np.median(purity):.0f}"`% of a population's country-years
are in its majority cluster, and the label changes in
`{python} f"{100 * switches:.0f}"`% of consecutive observed years.  A
population's deviation pattern persists from year to year, but it is not
fixed over the whole series.

# Part B — Level epochs

## The level signal and its direction

The level coordinate $\mathcal{G}_{c,t}[1,1]$ removed in Part A is used
here to describe *how fast mortality is changing* (the level epochs, which are in the
companion only).  Its sign
is that of the singular vectors $\mathbf{s}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_1$, which is a
convention: in this decomposition $\mathcal{G}_{c,t}[1,1]$ *falls* as e₀
rises, but another linear-algebra library or sign rule could flip it.  To
make "improvement" mean improvement whatever the convention, we multiply
the level coordinate by the sign of its correlation with e₀
(`mdmx.clustering.level_orientation`):

$$
\ell_{c,t} = \sigma\, \mathcal{G}_{c,t}[1,1], \qquad
\sigma = \operatorname{sign}\operatorname{corr}\bigl(\mathcal{G}_{c,t}[1,1],\, e_0\bigr),
$$

so that $\ell$ rises when mortality improves whatever the orientation of the
bases (with the decomposition chapter's orientation, $\sigma = +1$).  The
thresholds below are stated for $\ell$.  To express them in years of life expectancy, we regress e₀ on
$\ell$ across all observed country-years: one unit of $\ell$ corresponds to
$b$ years of e₀.

```{python}
#| label: c06-orientation
#| code-summary: "Orient the level signal by e0 and translate the thresholds into e0 units"
sigma = clus.level_orientation(level, e0)
ell = sigma * level
e0_per_ell, e0_at_zero = np.polyfit(ell, e0, 1)
print(f"σ = {sigma:+d}: the level coordinate G[1,1] {'falls' if sigma < 0 else 'rises'} as e0 rises")
print(f"e0 ≈ {e0_at_zero:.1f} + {e0_per_ell:.3f} ℓ   (R² = {np.corrcoef(ell, e0)[0, 1] ** 2:.3f})")
print(f"δ = {PE['delta']} ℓ/year ≈ {PE['delta'] * e0_per_ell:.3f} years of e0 per year; "
      f"δ_rapid = {PE['delta_rapid']} ℓ/year ≈ {PE['delta_rapid'] * e0_per_ell:.3f}")
latex.report("clusEpochWindow", PE["window"], desc="Epoch rolling-window width W (years)")
latex.report("clusEpochMinPoints", PE["min_points"], desc="Minimum observed years per window")
latex.report("clusEpochMinYears", PE["min_years"], desc="Minimum observed years for a population to be classified")
latex.report("clusEpochDelta", PE["delta"], digits=2, desc="Stagnation half-width delta (level units per year)")
latex.report("clusEpochDeltaRapid", PE["delta_rapid"], digits=2, desc="Rapid-change threshold (level units per year)")
latex.report("clusEpochLowessFrac", PE["lowess_frac"], digits=2, desc="LOWESS span (share of a population's years)")
latex.report("clusEpochLowessMinPoints", PE["lowess_min_points"], desc="Minimum LOWESS span (observed years)")
latex.report("clusEpochEzeroPerLevel", float(e0_per_ell), digits=2, desc="Years of e0 per unit of the level signal (OLS slope)")
latex.report("clusEpochDeltaEzero", float(PE["delta"] * e0_per_ell), digits=2,
             desc="delta translated into years of e0 per calendar year")
latex.report("clusEpochDeltaRapidEzero", float(PE["delta_rapid"] * e0_per_ell), digits=2,
             desc="delta_rapid translated into years of e0 per calendar year");
```

The translation is close to one-to-one: a stagnation band of
$|\text{slope}| \le \delta$ = `{python} f"{PE['delta']}"` level units per
year means e₀ changing by less than about
`{python} f"{PE['delta'] * e0_per_ell:.2f}"` years per year (half a year
per decade), and "rapid" change means more than about
`{python} f"{PE['delta_rapid'] * e0_per_ell:.2f}"` years of e₀ per year
(two years per decade).

## The classification

The procedure takes every setting from the parameter file:

1. **Smooth.**  For each population with at least
   `{python} f"{PE['min_years']}"` observed years, smooth $\ell$ and e₀
   over its observed years by LOWESS (`mdmx.clustering.lowess_at`), with a
   span of `{python} f"{PE['lowess_frac']}"` of the population's years but
   never fewer than `{python} f"{PE['lowess_min_points']}"` years, and
   `{python} f"{PE['lowess_iterations']}"` robustness iterations.
2. **Slopes.**  Slide a window of $W$ = `{python} f"{PE['window']}"`
   calendar years across the series one year at a time; in each window
   with at least `{python} f"{PE['min_points']}"` observed years, fit a
   least-squares line to the smoothed $\ell$ and keep its slope
   (`mdmx.clustering.window_slopes`).
3. **Classify** each window slope $s$: rapid improvement if
   $s > \delta_{\text{rapid}}$, slow improvement if
   $\delta < s \le \delta_{\text{rapid}}$, stagnation if $|s| \le \delta$,
   slow worsening if $-\delta_{\text{rapid}} \le s < -\delta$, rapid
   worsening if $s < -\delta_{\text{rapid}}$ (`classify_slopes`).
4. **Assign years.**  Each calendar year from the population's first to
   last observed year takes the most common category among the windows
   that contain it (`yearly_categories`, which uses `majority_label`);
   ties go to the category listed first above, i.e. towards rapid
   improvement.  Years in the middle of a series are covered by $W$
   windows; years near either end by fewer, so their category rests on
   less evidence.
5. **Epochs** are maximal runs of consecutive calendar years with the
   same category (`runs`).

```{python}
#| label: c06-epochs
#| code-summary: "Classify level epochs for every population"
ep = clus.classify_epochs(c_idx, obs_year, ell, e0, pops, **PE)
win, yrs_cat, epochs = ep["windows"], ep["years"], ep["epochs"]
epochs.insert(1, "name", epochs["pop"].map(NAME))
classified = yrs_cat[yrs_cat["category"] >= 0]
sign_agree = float(np.mean(np.sign(win["slope_level"]) == np.sign(win["slope_e0"])))
cat_share = classified["category"].value_counts(normalize=True).reindex(range(5), fill_value=0)
tie_share = float(classified["tied"].mean())
print(f"Populations classified: {yrs_cat['pop'].nunique()}; skipped (too few years): {ep['skipped'] or 'none'}")
print(f"Windows: {len(win):,}; calendar years classified: {len(classified):,}; "
      f"unclassified years inside a series: {int((yrs_cat['category'] < 0).sum())}")
print(f"Windows in which the level and e0 slopes have the same sign: {100 * sign_agree:.1f}%")
print(f"Calendar years decided by the tie-break: {100 * tie_share:.1f}%")
print("\nMedian e0 slope (years per year) of the windows in each category:")
print(win.groupby("category")["slope_e0"].median().rename(index=dict(enumerate(clus.EPOCH_CATEGORIES))).round(3))
print("\nShare of classified country-years and number of epochs by category:")
print(pd.DataFrame({"share of years": cat_share.to_numpy().round(3),
                    "epochs": epochs["category"].value_counts().reindex(range(5), fill_value=0).to_numpy()},
                   index=clus.EPOCH_CATEGORIES))
latex.report("clusEpochNPops", int(yrs_cat["pop"].nunique()), desc="Populations with level epochs")
latex.report("clusEpochNEpochs", int(len(epochs)), desc="Number of level epochs")
latex.report("clusEpochSignAgree", 100 * sign_agree, digits=1,
             desc="Percent of windows where level-signal and e0 slopes have the same sign")
latex.report("clusEpochTieShare", 100 * tie_share, digits=1, desc="Percent of classified years decided by the tie-break")
for code, key in enumerate(["RapidImp", "SlowImp", "Stag", "SlowWorse", "RapidWorse"]):
    latex.report(f"clusEpochShare{key}", 100 * float(cat_share[code]), digits=1,
                 desc=f"Percent of classified country-years in category '{clus.EPOCH_CATEGORIES[code]}'")
```

```{python}
for ax in axes[:, 0]:
    ax.set_ylabel("$e_0$ (years)")
```

```{python}
#| label: c06-epoch-text
#| code-summary: "Facts quoted in the text below"
worse = epochs[epochs["category"] >= 3]
worse_by_pop = worse.groupby("pop").agg(first=("start", "min"), last=("end", "max"), years=("n_years", "sum"))
def _span(first, last):
    """'1970' for a single year, '1972–1998' for a range."""
    return f"{first}" if first == last else f"{first}–{last}"

worse_text = "; ".join(f"{NAME[p_]} ({_span(r_['first'], r_['last'])}, "
                       f"{r_['years']} year{'s' if r_['years'] > 1 else ''})"
                       for p_, r_ in worse_by_pop.sort_values("first").iterrows())
usa_last = epochs[epochs["pop"] == "USA"].tail(3)
usa_text = ", ".join(f"{r_.label.lower()} {_span(r_.start, r_.end)}" for r_ in usa_last.itertuples())
usa_years = yrs_cat[yrs_cat["pop"] == "USA"]
usa_last_windows = int(usa_years["n_windows"].iloc[-1])
print("Worsening epochs:", worse_text)
print("Last three epochs of the United States:", usa_text)
latex.report("clusEpochShareWorse", 100 * float(cat_share[3] + cat_share[4]), digits=1,
             desc="Percent of classified country-years in a worsening category");
```

Improvement dominates: `{python} f"{100 * cat_share[0]:.0f}"`% of the
classified country-years are in rapid and
`{python} f"{100 * cat_share[1]:.0f}"`% in slow improvement,
`{python} f"{100 * cat_share[2]:.0f}"`% in stagnation and only
`{python} f"{100 * (cat_share[3] + cat_share[4]):.1f}"`% in worsening.
Stagnation marks the long pre-transition periods of the earliest series
(Sweden, France, England & Wales, Norway) and the Eastern European
plateau of the 1960s–1980s.  The worsening epochs are few and
recognisable: `{python} worse_text`.  The post-Soviet mortality crisis is
therefore captured.  For the United States the last three epochs are
`{python} usa_text`; the final year of a series is covered by only
`{python} f"{usa_last_windows}"` window (years near either end of a
series always rest on fewer windows than years in the middle), so the
recent slowdown of mortality improvement in the United States appears essentially as
stagnation rather than worsening.  Because the level and e₀ slopes agree
in sign in `{python} f"{100 * sign_agree:.1f}"`% of windows, the
direction assigned to each window is unambiguous almost everywhere.
